summary: Intro discovery for Redwood PLG quickstart. Stormbridge is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for generative features. Main asks: time-to-first-token, free credits/quickstart experience, security (SOC2/KMS/SSO), and cost/latency tradeoffs. transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on the PLG team. Quick intros?
[00:06] Alex Rivera: Alex here, CTO at Stormbridge. We run analytics and building a insights chat feature.
[00:10] Priya Srinivasan: Hi Priya, lead ML. We'll own integration.
[00:12] Sam Wu: Sam, infra. I'll be involved if we go dedicated or VPC.
[00:15] Jonah Patel: Jonah, SE at Redwood. I'll cover technical bits and perf.
[00:20] Dana Lee: Dana, Product. We'll drive success criteria.
[00:25] Maya Chen: Great. Goal for today is to understand your stack, timeline, success metrics and run through the quickstart experience - time to first token, what free credits look like, and high level hosted/dedicated/private decisions.
[01:02] Alex Rivera: For context - we currently call OpenAI for some generative jobs but running into cost and latency spikes. We're exploring alternatives that let us control latency and cost. Important for us: SOC2, SSO, and the ability to bench locally for dedicated numbers.
[01:24] Priya Srinivasan: On the ML side we care about throughput for batched prompts and maintaining deterministic-ish responses for a subset of workloads. Also curious on embeddings for semantic search.
[01:39] Sam Wu: From infra: if we go private we'd expect VPC peering and KMS integration, audit logs, and maybe on-prem later. Latency SLA matters - 99th pct under 300ms ideal.
[02:02] Jonah Patel: Totally, those are common asks. Quicknote on quickstart: our PLG flow gives free credits to spin up API keys and run sample calls. Most teams get first token in under 10 minutes if they follow the quickstart. We'll send sandbox creds after this call.
[02:25] Maya Chen: Free credits typically cover a couple thousand requests depending on model. For evaluation we recommend using our smaller open models first or a Redwood-verified model to measure baseline.
[02:50] Alex Rivera: How much effort to go from quickstart to real user traffic? If we start in hosted and later move to dedicated, is it seamless?
[03:05] Jonah Patel: The API is consistent across hosted/dedicated/private. You can pin model versions. Moving to dedicated is mostly an infra config change and migration of keys, but we'll want to run perf tests because dedicated pools have different batch/throughput characteristics. We do have routing and automatic fallback if capacity's constrained.
[03:40] Priya Srinivasan: Can you explain KV cache and batching behaviour? We have many short prompts; batching helps cost but hurts latency sometimes.
[03:55] Jonah Patel: Sure - KV cache stores key/value cache for autoregressive decode. For chat or long-context workloads it avoids recomputing past tokens. Our runtime supports dynamic batching; it will batch requests with small windows to optimize throughput while honoring latency SLOs. For short prompts you can tune max_batch_delay and target latency.
[04:32] Sam Wu: Any note on quantization or kernel selection? We use a mix of 16-bit and int8 on some models.
[04:41] Jonah Patel: We recommend model/quantization profiles per workload. Our Optimize tool suggests quant settings and kernel choices based on seq length distribution. We'll share a recommendation doc.
[05:00] Dana Lee: Security: Alex mentioned SOC2. Are you SOC2 certified? What about SSO and HSM/KMS options for private?
[05:12] Maya Chen: Redwood is SOC2 compliant (we'll send the attestation). For Private deployments you can integrate customer-managed KMS/HSM and VPC peering; audit logs are available. SSO via SAML/OIDC is supported for the console and API access control via RBAC.
[05:36] Alex Rivera: Good. We need to know data residency options too - region control for EU data.
[05:44] Maya Chen: Yes, you can pick regions for Dedicated/Private. Hosted is in multiple regions; we can talk about EU-only tenancy if needed.
[06:00] Priya Srinivasan: About benchmarking - what's the best way to get numbers that match our production patterns?
[06:08] Jonah Patel: If you can share a small sample trace of prompts and seq lengths we can produce a perf estimate. We'll also share a lightweight benchmark script you can run against the quickstart sandbox. That usually surfaces cost/latency tradeoffs and helps decide if Dedicated or Hosted is right.
[06:35] Alex Rivera: For cost - can you give a rough comparison? We care about per-token cost at scale.
[06:42] Maya Chen: Hosted has the simplest path with pay-as-you-go pricing; dedicated gives lower unit costs at commit tiers with reserved capacity. Private has higher fixed costs but better isolation and potential lower incremental cost at large scale. We'll send a pricing example for 100k tokens/day.
[07:05] Sam Wu: Anything else around networking for private? We prefer private link or VPC peering, not direct internet egress for model traffic.
[07:14] Jonah Patel: VPC peering/private link is standard for Private; we can outline IP ranges and connection requirements in the security pack.
[07:28] Alex Rivera: If we do quickstart now, do we get real API keys or sandbox only? We want realistic latency numbers.
[07:36] Maya Chen: You get sandbox keys mapped to hosted endpoints. They are production-like but sometimes on shared pools; for exact production numbers we recommend a short dedicated pilot or running targeted workloads on hosted and then replicating on dedicated for comparison.
[08:00] Priya Srinivasan: On embeddings - how do you handle vector storage? Do you provide managed vectors or do we handle storage?
[08:10] Jonah Patel: We have an embeddings API; vector storage is customer-managed by default, but we also offer managed vector store add-ons. For quickstart we suggest pushing embeddings to your vector DB and running similarity tests.
[08:28] Dana Lee: Regarding timelines - we hope to have an initial POC by end of month. Is that feasible?
[08:35] Maya Chen: Yes, with quickstart and free credits you can be validating basic flows within a week. For a dedicated pilot we'd align timelines after the POC scoping call.
[09:00] Alex Rivera: Any red flags or common pitfalls you've seen?
[09:05] Jonah Patel: Common issues: batch sizing too aggressive causing latency spikes, not pinning model versions leading to eval drift, and forgetting to instrument token-level cost in early testing. We help with recommendations and monitoring dashboards.
[09:30] Priya Srinivasan: About monitoring - do you provide token-level breakdowns per route?
[09:36] Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood Console has per-route token and latency breakdowns, tracing hooks and rollouts. You can set alerts on quality regressions and cost anomalies.
[09:50] Sam Wu: For private/on-prem, what's the support model? We may need 24/7 for initial rollout.
[09:59] Luis Ortega: Our support tiers include enterprise on-call for private deployments. We'll attach support options in the follow-up.
[10:12] Alex Rivera: Great. Can you show an example of the quickstart code? We like Node and Python.
[10:18] Jonah Patel: Sure - basic curl example: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>' -d '{"model":"redwood-base-1","input":"Hello"}' - most SDKs take about 3 lines. We'll add a nailed-down code sample in the email.
[11:05] Dana Lee: Any gotchas with rate limits in the sandbox?
[11:09] Maya Chen: Sandbox has conservative rate limits; if you need higher concurrency for benchmarking we'll open burst capacity or provide a short-term dedicated test pool.
[11:30] Alex Rivera: On the compliance docs - send SOC2, ISO, and a sample DPA. Also want network diagrams for VPC peering.
[11:42] Maya Chen: Noted - will send security pack with attestation and network diagrams.
[12:00] Priya Srinivasan: For the POC scoping - can we include a small benchmark: 1k requests/min, average seq 120 tokens, 50% embedding usage?
[12:10] Jonah Patel: Yes we'll model that and return estimated latency and cost.
[12:32] Dana Lee: Ok let's recap next steps.
[12:35] Maya Chen: Recap: we'll send quickstart guide and sandbox creds, security pack (SOC2/ISO/DPA/network diagrams), Jonah will share a benchmark script and suggested quant/profile, and we'll schedule POC scoping with your infra for next week.
[12:52] Alex Rivera: Sounds good.
[13:00] Maya Chen: Thanks all. We'll follow up by EOD with the assets.
[13:10] Sam Wu: Thanks.
[13:15] End of recording.
